qc.label_under_test: something standing in for the real thing: an actor playing a role, an imaginary or fictional figure, a pretend object; the same scenes with real people and objects stay quiet
qc.notes: Picked for its link to the analogy map (a vehicle stands in for something). The current label includes 'a pretend object', but probes of six physical stand-ins (a replica crown, a stunt double, a toy sword, a wax figure, a decoy duck, a cardboard cutout) all read 0.01-0.03. This refine keeps roles and invented things and moves physical copies to the near misses. I read this pole's earlier test before writing mine (the brief asks to read it after drafting): none of its sentences or frames are reused, and these 16 sentences were scored 0 times before this commit.

neighbours.label: an invented or pretended role or thing: the token after 'plays a' / 'portrays a' / 'voices a', or the words 'fictional', 'imaginary', 'make-believe'; PHYSICAL stand-ins for a real thing (replicas, toys, wax figures, decoys, cardboard cutouts, stunt doubles) stay quiet
fire: In the new film, Meryl Streep plays a lighthouse keeper on a remote island.
The podcast follows a fictional mayor through one chaotic week.
My daughter keeps an imaginary dragon under her bed.
In the school play, Sam portrays a grumpy old king.
The comic is set in a fictional town on the Welsh coast.
The mime climbed an imaginary ladder in the square.
For the radio drama, the actor voices a retired sea captain.
The children built a make-believe castle out of blankets.
quiet: In the new film, a stunt double jumps from the lighthouse on a remote island.
The museum displays a replica of the mayor's carriage from 1890.
My daughter keeps a plastic dragon under her bed.
In the school play, Sam carries a cardboard crown for the old king.
The comic is set in a real town on the Welsh coast.
The mime climbed a wooden ladder in the square.
For the radio drama, the actor brought a recording of a sea captain.
The children built a toy castle out of plastic blocks.
neighbours.short: pretended or invented (a role, a fictional or imaginary thing), not a physical copy
